Manufacturing of the two tunnel boring machines that will be used for the Palisades Tunnel Project is complete.
Each tunnel boring machine's cutterhead is nearly 29 feet in diameter.

TBM S-1432 assembled at the factory for testing.

Installing rebar in the HYCC-3 trench in preparation for upcoming concrete pours.
Excavation and construction of the portal launch box at the base of the Palisades where the first two tunnel boring machines will be assembled.
We completed the Tonnelle Ave bridge structure, opening the passage beneath the highway that will be used to bring the TBM components in for assembly.
Construction of a slurry wall panel for the 12th Avenue Access Shaft. Seven slurry wall panels have been completed so far.
Snow on the ground highlights the outline of the Hudson County Access Shaft in Weehawken. The circumference of this shaft is more than 400 feet.
The view from the eastern end of the HYCC-3 trench. Sections of the concrete floor and walls of the tunnel box are visible below the yellow struts that support the sides of the trench.
Marine temporary structures in the water just off Manhattan enable ground stabilization beneath the bulkhead.
Installation of a slurry wall panel for the Hudson County Access Shaft.
Excavation in preparation for the arrival of the first set of tunnel boring machines is visible under the new Tonnelle Avenue bridge.
A king pile is pulled from the western side of the cofferdam. It will be reinstalled on the eastern side to shift the enclosed area toward Manhattan.
The Tonnelle Avenue bridge is almost finished. The team is building the eastern bridge deck and there is clearance below the highway for the tunnel boring machines.
The Hudson River Ground Stabilization team has finished mixing 378 primary columns and 309 secondary columns of reinforced earth in the riverbed.
The HYCC-3 team completed the first major concrete pour of the project, pouring 4,500 cubic yards of concrete to form the tunnel box.
Ten of the 42 panels that will make up the slurry wall of the Hudson County Access Shaft have been completed.
Work to get ready for underground construction is ongoing on both sides of 12th Avenue - and in the river.
The Tonnelle Avenue Project will be finished soon, clearing the way for the first set of tunnel boring machines to be brought to the launch point in New Jersey.
The cofferdam containing the Hudson River Ground Stabilization Project work area is moving closer to Manhattan as the team makes progress on stabilizing the riverbed.
The HYCC-3 team installed liner wall inside the trench and prepared to pour concrete to form the floor of the tunnel box.
The noise barrier around the Hudson County Access Shaft construction site is now in place.
The 12th Avenue Access Shaft is taking shape in Manhattan. This 130-foot-wide, 80-foot-deep shaft will enable underground construction beneath 12th Avenue and W. 30th Street.
For the first time ever, you can see daylight under Tonnelle Avenue. The first construction package of the Hudson Tunnel Project is almost done!
The HRGS team started work removing the submerged remains of Pier 68 to clear the path for the tunnel boring machines.
The HYCC-3 team installs struts, tiebacks, and walers to hold up the walls of the trench during excavation and tunnel box construction.
We installed a barrier along the edge of the Hudson County Shaft construction site to reduce noise from the work site.
Guide walls for the 12th Avenue Shaft are being installed, showing the scale of this massive access shaft.

CEO Tom Prendergast shows FTA Administrator Marc Molinaro and FRA Senior Advisor David Fink the progress we have made across five active construction sites in the year since securing full funding for the project.
Traffic on Tonnelle Avenue was shifted onto the newly-built middle section of the bridge. This marked the transition into the final phase of this project.
The team started shifting the cofferdam east so stabilization can proceed on a new section of the riverbed. Deep Soil Mixing continues inside the cofferdam.
CEO Tom Prendergast speaks to reporters during a media tour of the five active HTP construction projects.
A worker on the HYCC-3 Project installs support of excavation infrastructure to hold up the walls of the trench while excavation progresses.

The Hudson County Shaft has started to take shape. This shaft that will be used to replace the tunnel boring machines that dig the New Jersey section of the tunnel with the machines that will dig under the Hudson River.
Construction of the Manhattan Tunnel Project kicked off with the demolition of existing structures and removal of underground obstructions at the work site.
The team working on the Palisades Tunnel Project built a massive access ramp to enable support of excavation work around the tunnel boring machine launch point.
Crews relocated the gas main that runs beside Tonnelle Avenue, enabling the final stage of bridge construction to begin.
The team reached the halfway point of the HYCC-3 project on schedule. More than 400,000 tons of soil and 1 million gallons of water have been removed.
Work on the Manhattan Tunnel Project has started. Investigatory geotechnical boring is in progress to collect data on soil and rock conditions before construction of the 12th Avenue shaft begins.
GDC CEO Tom Prendergast speaks to members of Congress during a tour of the active construction sites in Manhattan.
Construction of the center portion of the bridge continues at Tonnelle Avenue.
Heavy equipment has started to arrive at the Palisades Tunnel Project site as prep work for tunnel boring continues to ramp up, including the start of soldier pile installation.
Excavation and dewatering of the trench that will hold the HYCC-3 tunnel box continues. Struts are installed to support the sides of the trench during excavation.

blueskyPosts.text: Our Chief of Program Delivery and Chief Engineer took CNN's Richard Quest on a tour of our construction site in the Hudson River to explain the ground stabilization work we're doing to prepare the riverbed for tunnel boring. Watch the segment to learn more about this important work!

In the 1800s, dirt and rubble were used to extend Manhattan's shoreline. To prepare for tunnel boring through this fill, we're installing pipes in Hudson River Park that will circulate cold brine underground, freezing the loose material into a solid block that is easier to tunnel through.

George has been a member of IUOE Local 825 for 25 years. Now he's leading a team working on the Palisades Tunnel Project. He and his crew are proud to show up and work hard to build one of the biggest infrastructure projects in the country.

Colin is part of a family of builders who helped make New York City what it is today. Now he's making his mark as a member of the team building the Hudson Tunnel Project. It's that sense of legacy and the pride that comes from building something lasting that drives the workforce behind this project.

For Ronald, working on the Manhattan Tunnel Project isn't just a job, it's a chance to do something important for everybody who travels into, out of, and through New York City. It's hard work - especially in the winter - but that sense of purpose, and his great coworkers, are why he loves the job.

We're pouring concrete for the third and final section of the Hudson Yards Concrete Casing! The tunnel floor is finished, and we're making progress on the walls. When it's complete, the concrete casing will connect the new tunnel to New York Penn Station.
We're almost finished installing the slurry wall for the Hudson County Access Shaft! Once that wall is complete, we'll begin excavating the 120-foot-deep shaft.

Workers are back on the job in Manhattan and in the Hudson River! We're continuing installation of the slurry wall for the 12th Avenue Access Shaft and stabilizing the riverbed to prepare for tunnel boring.

Construction is resuming at all our sites this week. At the tunnel portal in North Bergen, we're continuing construction of the launch box where the tunnel boring machines will be assembled and start tunneling. The components of the first machine are on site, ready for assembly!

Construction of the Hudson Tunnel Project is resuming! Workers who have been impacted by the construction pause are returning to our construction sites this week. 

More info here: www.gatewayprogram.org/wp-content/u...

Rudy Duarte is one of the hundreds of union workers impacted by the Hudson Tunnel Project construction pause. His message is clear: fund this urgent project now so workers like him can get back to work building the modern, reliable infrastructure America needs.

The Gateway Development Commission will hold an in-person public Board Meeting on Tuesday, February 24, 2026, at 10:00 am. Registration and public comment information can be found here: www.gatewayprogram.org/board-meetin...

"I had to let all my guys go. There's no checks coming in for them."

Guido Rivieccio, one of the shop stewards working on the Manhattan Tunnel Project, describes the real-world impact that pausing funding for the Hudson Tunnel Project had on the workers on his team this week.

Hundreds of workers should be on site building the Hudson Tunnel Project this week. Instead, we had to put up these signs at our construction sites because we still cannot access the federal funding for the project. Funding must be restored now so we can get back to work!

Pausing construction of the Hudson Tunnel Project hurts hundreds of workers. More than 200 union workers rallied at GDC's North Bergen construction site earlier this week to call for federal funding to be restored so they can get back to work.

When work pauses, paychecks stop. LIUNA General President Brent Booker explains to NJ Spotlight that withholding funding for the Hudson Tunnel Project means lost income, fewer dollars in local economies, and workers struggling to make ends meet.

The pause in federal funding for the Hudson Tunnel Project threatens the livelihoods of hundreds of workers. Local 472 member Lamont Richardson told NY1 what's at stake for his union brothers and sisters.

We've already put more than $1 billion and countless hours into construction of the Hudson Tunnel Project. We have active construction sites across New York and New Jersey, and we're ready to start tunnel boring. Funding must be restored now so we can keep building.
Stopping construction of the Hudson Tunnel Project will hurt our regional and national economy. An extended construction pause would put nearly 100,000 total jobs at risk.

Construction of the Hudson Tunnel Project will be suspended today if disbursements of federal funding obligated to the project do not resume. 

More information about the impacts of pausing construction and our ongoing efforts to restore funding here: www.gatewayprogram.org/wp-content/u...

Nearly 1,000 workers will lose their jobs immediately when construction of the Hudson Tunnel Project pauses tomorrow, and an extended pause will put many more jobs at risk.

Funding must be restored ASAP so these hardworking men and women can get back to work.

"Superstorm Sandy showed us that at any moment, we could be shut down. And if we're shut down, we're screwed."

Steve Valeira discussed the stakes of stopping construction of the Hudson Tunnel Project at our Board Meeting last week.

Watch his statement here: www.youtube.com/live/aUxLY39...

"If we don't work, we don't get paid, and playing politics does not put food on the table for us."
 
Davon Lomax shared how stopping construction will impact the thousands of men and women building the Hudson Tunnel Project.
 
Watch his statement at our Board Meeting: www.youtube.com/live/aUxLY39...

"We're already 10,000 yards plus of concrete into this job. Why waste it?"
 
At our Board Meeting, Teamster Raymond Klein highlighted the progress already made by the hundreds of workers who will lose their jobs if funding for the Hudson Tunnel Project isn't restored.

"I urge everyone involved: Please find a solution to keep this project moving. We're all depending on you."

Robert Fawcett spoke out for the workers who will lose their jobs if construction of the Hudson Tunnel Project pauses at our Board Meeting.

Watch his testimony: youtu.be/YcjFycSlEAs?...

We're ready to build! The components of the first tunnel boring machine are on site in North Bergen, ready to be assembled in the portal launch box. Federal funding disbursements must resume ASAP so we can start tunneling.

Delays like this will become more frequent - and impact more riders - the longer we rely on the North River Tunnel. We need to complete the Hudson Tunnel Project as soon as possible to deliver reliable, modern rail infrastructure that riders can count on. 

www.bloomberg.com/news/article...

"President Donald Trump, free this money up now, so I can get to work and make my neighborhood better." 

Ironworker John Mooney spoke for the hundreds of workers building the Hudson Tunnel Project at our Board Meeting. 

Watch his full testimony here: youtu.be/YcjFycSlEAs?...

The Newsday Editorial Board is right: the Hudson Tunnel Project is the most important rail project in the country, for workers, riders, and our economy. Federal funding must be restored so construction can continue. 

Read the whole editorial here: www.newsday.com/opinion/edit...

Snow and ice don't stop us. The hundreds of hardworking men and women building the Hudson Tunnel Project show up every day and endure the elements to deliver the most urgent passenger rail project in the country. Federal funding must be restored so these workers can stay on the job.

The Hudson Tunnel Project is the most urgent infrastructure project in the country - for workers, riders, and the economy - and funding must be restored now. That's the message we heard loud and clear from workers building the tunnel at our Board Meeting yesterday.
Today GDC notified our contractors that construction of the Hudson Tunnel Project will pause on February 6 if federal funding disbursements do not resume.
Major delivery in North Bergen! The main drive unit for the first tunnel boring machine has arrived at our construction site. Most of the components for this TBM are now on site.

No missed connections here! We recently broke through the bulkhead separating the part of the Hudson Yards Concrete Casing being built under the High Line from the section that is already complete. We're now one step closer to connecting the new tunnel under the Hudson River to Penn Station.

The Gateway Development Commission will hold an in-person public Board Meeting on Tuesday, January 27, 2026, at 10:00 am. Registration and public comment information can be found here: www.gatewayprogram.org/board-meetin....

We're more than halfway finished installing the slurry wall for the Hudson County Access Shaft. This underground concrete wall will support the sides of the shaft during excavation.

Learn more and see our progress on our live construction camera at www.gatewayprogram.org/palisades-tu...

We're continuing to make progress toward the start of tunnel boring! While our tunnel boring machines are in transit from the factory, our team in New Jersey has been hard at work building the portal launch box at the foot of the Palisades. Next step: assembling the TBMs on site!

New year, new look. We just installed a fence wrap around our construction site on 12th Avenue. You can see the work happening here, and at our other sites in Manhattan, from the High Line near Hudson Yards. We also have live feeds of all five active construction sites at www.gatewayprogram.org

Last week, the HYCC-3 team completed a second major concrete pour. We poured more than 2,700 cubic yards of concrete for a section of the "invert slab," the floor of the tunnel box.

Learn more about the HYCC-3 Project at www.gatewayprogram.org/hudson-yards...

We made a lot of progress in 2025!

We manufactured our first two tunnel boring machines, opened the passage under Tonnelle Ave, passed the halfway point on HYCC-3, and much more. 

Click the link to see the latest pictures from our construction sites: www.gatewayprogram.org/photo-galler...

Happy holidays from GDC! From the portal launch box in New Jersey to the concrete casing in Manhattan, the thousands of construction workers on the Hudson Tunnel Project made significant progress on both sides of the Hudson River this year.

Before tunnel boring machines can dig under the Hudson River, the riverbed must be stabilized. That's a huge project on its own. We have to create a block of reinforced earth more than four city blocks long!

Learn how we're getting the job done at www.gatewayprogram.org/hudson-river...

The latest edition of The GDC Gazette is here! 📰

In this issue:
1. Photos and video of our first tunnel boring machines.
2. A look inside our new Community Engagement Center.
3. Updates on our five active construction projects.

Read the newsletter here: mailchi.mp/gatewayprogr...

Tunnel boring machines are not standard-issue construction equipment. Each TBM that we use for the Hudson Tunnel Project is a highly complex machine, custom-built for this project. The TBM in this video is on its way to New Jersey now. We'll reassemble it on site and start tunnel boring next year.

Next stop: tunnel boring! 

We've finished manufacturing the first set of tunnel boring machines for the Hudson Tunnel Project. The machines are shipping to New Jersey now, and tunnel boring will start next  year.

Read the full announcement here: www.gatewayprogram.org/wp-content/u...
